purpose: Public claim-level quality evidence. Every card names its evidence class, result date, reproduction sources, owner, limitation, and visible non-pass boundary.

cards.claim: A new developer can reach one useful Project -> Task fixture state from the recorded source revision without a provider credential.

reproduction.artifact_contract: A clean local source checkout produces an isolated .abproj workspace, fixture-run artifacts, and browser-visible task graph state.
reproduction.test_command: Follow docs/NO_KEY_FIRST_TEN_MINUTES.md exactly; its recorded proof is for the named source revision.

known_limitations: The proof is for one exact source revision and Windows toolchain.
It does not prove a public installer, live provider/model behavior, tool authority, or coding-route eligibility.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: The guide requires an isolated no-key path and names the failed earlier dependency attempt plus the exact non-claims.

cards.claim: A bounded code-fix/test/review workflow exposes task state, approval-gated write semantics, a deliberate failure, and retry recovery without a provider credential.

reproduction.artifact_contract: The runner emits a secret-free evidence packet with dry-run, expected fixture failure, blocked downstream nodes, and recovered fixture run.

known_limitations: It is not a live provider response, authorized coding route, autonomous code write, tool-authority, or installer proof.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: The evidence packet must contain a failed fixture run before the retry-recovery pass.

cards.claim: Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi K3, and GLM route metadata and deterministic adapter contracts are inspectable without being promoted to coding-route authority.

reproduction.artifact_contract: The cohort emits a secret-free route report with provider_calls_attempted=false, network_calls_attempted=false, and per-route authority state.

known_limitations: All four current routes remain review_only, no_tools, ask, and reduced_authority.
Live provider smoke, tool contract, coding-route verification, and default-route eligibility remain deferred.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: Each route card shows review_only / reduced_authority and the exact next evidence gate.

cards.claim: One native Code Fix / Test / Review graph round-trips through the GUI/runtime subset with source ownership and approval boundaries preserved.

reproduction.artifact_contract: The runner emits source graph, GUI surface, runtime manifest, semantic diff, and secret-free evidence with no_change round-trip status.

known_limitations: Only the named native JSON graph and supported subset are covered.
It does not prove universal graph conversion, source-file write-back, live provider behavior, autonomous writes, or tool authority.

The broader task-graph HTTP API suite previously hung in test_http_api_lists_templates_instantiates_graph_and_updates_node_and_edge; this card claims only the focused parity evidence while the default stability owner retains that integration gap.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: Unsupported transformations must report loss or reject; direct source-owned GUI edits are expected to block. The dossier also records the unresolved broader HTTP-suite hang rather than claiming a full suite pass.

cards.claim: A newcomer can validate one bounded candidate skill manifest and see authority widening fail closed.

reproduction.artifact_contract: The runner emits lint/compile/dry-run results, lifecycle warnings, and a structured blocked allowlist-widening request without provider, MCP, or agent execution.

known_limitations: The example remains experimental candidate status and preserves lifecycle and route warnings.
It does not enable a plugin, install a skill, qualify a provider, grant tool/write authority, or permit merge-ready external code.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: The report records candidate warnings and blocks a request outside the manifest allowlist.

cards.claim: AstraBridge's source and preview evidence retain explicit isolation, credential-redaction, and sensitive-reporting boundaries.

reproduction.artifact_contract: The hardening scan reports only aggregate counts and findings; public evidence must remain secret-free.

known_limitations: No private vulnerability-reporting route, supported-version policy, or private conduct-reporting route is configured for a public preview.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: The security and conduct policies explicitly state the missing private routes instead of inventing a contact.

cards.claim: Release identity, deterministic staging, and an isolated Windows update transaction can be reproduced locally without being misrepresented as a published installer.

reproduction.artifact_contract: The gates emit release-readiness, update-rehearsal, and compact baseline evidence with the public_release result fixed to blocked until owner gates resolve.

known_limitations: No public binary, signed distribution, live update service, or supported-version table exists.
License/contribution terms, private reporting contacts, safe support intake, and authorized distribution remain release blockers.
Deep Windows artifact roots can exceed the staging path-length limit; use documented short roots until the release owner hardens that path.

failure_visibility.how_to_detect: The baseline aggregator emits public_release=blocked plus five named owner gates.
